anchor_goal: Understand the product rule and chain rule in calculus derivatives

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: Can you explain when I should use the product rule versus the chain rule when taking derivatives?

turns.speaker: Tutor
turns.text: Sure! Use the product rule when differentiating two multiplying functions f(x)*g(x). Use the chain rule for composite functions f(g(x)).

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: Got it. So for x^2 * sin(x), that's a product rule problem?

turns.speaker: Tutor
turns.text: Exactly. You differentiate x^2 times sin(x) plus x^2 times the derivative of sin(x), which gives 2x*sin(x) + x^2*cos(x).

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: Math always gives me a headache. What energy drinks do you drink when studying late?

turns.speaker: Tutor
turns.text: I usually stick to green tea or yerba mate because energy drinks like Red Bull cause a bad crash.

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: Have you played that new RPG game Elden Ring? Staying up late playing it destroyed my sleep schedule.

turns.speaker: Tutor
turns.text: Yes, Elden Ring is notoriously addictive! The boss fights require intense pattern memorization.
